title: Pluggable network-fault simulator + deterministic scenario runner
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Our current load/perf regression harness runs on best-effort network emulation (tc/netem) inside CI VMs which leads to high variance and flakiness for tail-latency and packet-loss sensitive scenarios. This makes debugging regressions across infrastructure changes time-consuming.
goals: Introduce a pluggable network-fault simulator API for the harness so scenarios can declare deterministic network profiles (delay/jitter/loss/bandwidth/partition).
Ship a lightweight Rust-based plugin with a noop fallback to reduce dependency surface and improve isolation from CI host config.
Add deterministic scenario manifests and a seed manager so runs are reproducible across machines and across months.
Expose network profile telemetry to the perf dashboard and include automated regression checks for tail latency and resends.
acceptance_criteria: Harness supports a --network-profile flag that accepts built-in profiles and plugin URIs.
At least one Rust plugin is implemented and exercised by nightly perf regression runs.
Replaying an archived scenario with the same manifest+seed yields equivalent p95/p99 latency within 5% on an isolated runner.
No regressions introduced to CI median runtime (>2% measured across 20 runs).
Confluence design doc and API spec published and linked from the ticket.

progress_updates: 2025-02-02: Kickoff meeting. Agreed plugin ABI will be a shared-memory control plane + UNIX socket command channel to avoid elevated privileges. Action items: prototype shim vs direct netem calls.

2025-02-10: Prototype Rust plugin v0.1 implemented. Uses tokio 1.22 and a small BPF-based sampler for packet timing. Observed +8% CPU on runner; investigating optimistic batching to reduce overhead. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/pull/1842

2025-02-18: Design review feedback from infra: prefer noop fallback instead of failing harness if plugin not available. Updated API spec in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PERF/Network+Plugin+Spec

2025-02-24: Reproducibility experiment 1/3 completed. Replaying historic scenario A with new plugin produced p99 within 3% of archived baseline; p95 varied by 7% due to host scheduling on CI—plan to isolate using reserved cores in further runs.

2025-03-01: Security/appsec asked for review of plugin code path due to socket use; added minimal auth token negotiation and bound socket to harness user. Marked security_review_required: false after team discussion but will route small PR for quick scan. Issue: depends on ENG-39321 for deterministic seeding library.

2025-03-03: Merged harness loader + manifest changes to feature branch. Next: land Rust plugin optimizations to reduce CPU overhead (switch to smol runtime for lower scheduler overhead) and add telemetry hooks.
risks: Runtime overhead: the plugin may add non-trivial CPU/latency overhead on shared CI runners. Mitigation: noop mode, optional sampling, and explicit runner labels for performance-sensitive runs.
Portability: netem-equivalent behavior across our GCP + on-prem fleet may differ. Mitigation: profile suite across representative nodes and document differences.
Maintenance: introducing ABI and native plugins increases maintenance burden. Mitigation: strict compatibility versioning and a single canonical Rust plugin maintained by infra/benchmarks squad.
